statement: US hyperscalers are revising 2026 capital-expenditure guidance upward: CoreWeave raised its 2026 capex to $31-35 billion (roughly double the $14.9 billion spent in 2025), following prior-week hikes by Meta, Google and Microsoft, and the four largest US hyperscalers are on track for ~$725 billion combined 2026 capex, up ~77% from ~$410 billion in 2025 with ~75% AI-directed.
why: AI buildout plus higher component costs (DRAM contract prices projected +13-18% QoQ and NAND +10-15% QoQ in Q3 2026) are pushing budgets up, with builders raising the low end of ranges rather than cutting.

impact.mechanism: Upward capex revisions channel more spend into AI GPUs and datacenter buildout, a direct demand tailwind across the compute stack.

evidence.source: The Tech Capital / Yahoo Finance / The Globe and Mail
evidence.excerpt: CoreWeave became the latest data-centre builder to raise its 2026 capex guidance, following hikes from Meta, Google and Microsoft the prior week, all citing higher component costs

confidence.basis: Secondary aggregation (page returned HTTP 403) corroborated by Yahoo Finance and Globe and Mail within one fetched document.
